purpose: Live Power Stack thematic radar; dynamically ranked by freshness/materiality and current market significance. Theme rank changes research priority, not company fundamental scores.

environment.label: Global duration + energy-inflation collision
environment.summary: US and Japanese long yields are at multi-decade highs while crude and especially refined-product tightness remain inflationary. Physical AI/grid demand is still strong, but the cost of capital has become an operating variable: the best themes must now clear financing, valuation and execution hurdles as well as demand.

whatIsNewNow: US 10Y is ~5.19%, US 30Y ~5.48% and Japan 10Y ~3.115%: global duration stress has intensified rather than normalized.
Oil/product inflation has re-entered the rates story. Distillate inventories remain structurally tight even as crude stocks rose, making refined products a cleaner inflation signal than crude alone.
The Trump-Xi meeting extended the trade truce but did not verify durable breakthroughs on rare-earth access, tariffs or advanced-technology/AI restrictions.
AI physical demand remains real, but 5%+ long rates make funded/contracted capacity and sponsor quality more important than announced MW.
Tesla Semi deliveries add genuine commercialization evidence, but not enough disclosed production/pricing economics to change the TSLA fundamental score.
China/HK AI infrastructure is broadening into optical interconnect and silicon-photonics equipment; treat new listings as differentiated research, not chase candidates.
Robotics commercialization remains strongest in fixed/warehouse automation and cobots; humanoid capital-market enthusiasm is being disciplined by regulators and weak installed-volume evidence.
whatMattersMostToMarketsNow: Global long-end yields and real financing costs
Refined-product/diesel inflation and Middle East supply risk
AI financing quality and realizable funded MW
Farm input affordability and crop/input ratios

themes.name: Global Duration / Capital Scarcity + Energy-Inflation Feedback
themes.whyNow: US 10Y ~5.19%, US 30Y ~5.48% and Japan 10Y ~3.115% coincide with renewed oil/product inflation. The market is facing both a higher risk-free rate and an inflation impulse rather than one offsetting the other.
themes.marketTransmission: equity multiples, housing, project finance, AI capex hurdle rates, USD, gold, credit, infrastructure valuation
themes.confirmation: long yields stay above 5% while oil/product prices remain elevated and Fed tightening expectations persist
themes.invalidation: inflation/growth cool enough for long yields and energy-product prices to fall sustainably together
themes.nextTest: US data, Treasury supply/auctions, Fed pricing and whether oil/product inflation persists
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: raise entry hurdle for duration/capex-heavy names; demand valuation discount or superior contracted cash-flow visibility

themes.name: Refined Products / Diesel Inflation + Middle East Supply Risk
themes.whyNow: US commercial crude stocks rose, but distillate stocks fell to ~107.4M barrels and remain structurally tight. Diesel scarcity and Middle East disruption can transmit into freight, farm margins and inflation even when crude inventories look less alarming.
themes.marketTransmission: headline/core inflation, freight, agriculture margins, refining, tanker economics, consumer purchasing power, Fed expectations
themes.confirmation: distillate inventories/cracks and freight stay elevated independently of crude
themes.invalidation: product inventories rebuild and cracks/freight normalize together
themes.nextTest: EIA product inventories, same-contract ULSD/RBOB cracks, refinery utilization and Middle East flows
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: XOM remains quality hold; MISC/HIBISCS stay hold/no-chase until company and price confirmation

themes.name: AI Credit / Financing Dispersion + Realizable MW
themes.whyNow: Physical AI demand remains strong but 5%+ long yields raise project-finance, sponsor and refinancing hurdles. Announced capacity deserves less weight than funded, contracted and energizable capacity.
themes.marketTransmission: AI capex, sponsor leverage, corporate/project spreads, data-centre timelines, infrastructure multiples
themes.confirmation: strong sponsors fund at acceptable spreads while weaker projects require concessions, guarantees or delays
themes.invalidation: AI credit spreads normalize broadly and funded FCF conversion improves across projects
themes.nextTest: new issuance/project-finance pricing, sponsor guarantees, contracted load and energization milestones
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: prefer cash-generative/contracted exposures; YTLPOWR requires funding + grid/self-supply + FCF proof before adding

themes.name: AI Infrastructure / Grid / Power / Cooling / Optical Interconnect
themes.whyNow: Grid access, generation, switchgear, wire/cable, cooling and optical connectivity remain physical bottlenecks. China/HK listings are widening the opportunity set into optical transceivers and silicon-photonics equipment, but valuations require discipline.
themes.marketTransmission: generation, transmission, switchgear, cooling, fiber/optical networking, water, permitting, data-centre commissioning
themes.confirmation: funded backlog, signed customers, interconnection/self-supply and FCF conversion
themes.invalidation: cancellations, utilization shortfalls or rapid shortage normalization
themes.nextTest: supplier backlog/pricing, energised MW, grid interconnections and economics of new HK optical/automation listings
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: PWR/ETN remain high-quality but price-sensitive; research Ligent/RoboTechnik branches without chasing

themes.name: Critical Minerals / Rare Earth / Copper Supply Security
themes.whyNow: The US-China truce extension did not verify resolution of rare-earth access. Yttrium bottlenecks remain strategically relevant to jet engines, power equipment and semiconductor manufacturing while copper/electrical demand stays tied to grid buildout.
themes.marketTransmission: aerospace, semiconductors, power equipment, defense, electrification capex, commodity pricing
themes.confirmation: persistent physical tightness, strategic procurement/offtake and supply diversification investment
themes.invalidation: verified durable export normalization plus falling physical premia/inventories rebuilding
themes.nextTest: rare-earth/yttrium export data, government procurement, copper inventories and grid demand
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: FCX remains active at disciplined prices; avoid conflating strategic scarcity with automatic miner upside

themes.name: AI Security / Governance
themes.whyNow: Commercial AI-security products and governance/evaluation services are turning the theme into recurring-spend mechanisms rather than generic AI fear. The challenge is valuation after strong price moves.
themes.marketTransmission: cybersecurity budgets, recurring ARR, model testing/governance, enterprise software mix
themes.confirmation: ARR/bookings, renewals and AI-security attach rates accelerate
themes.invalidation: spend remains experimental, low-value or commoditized
themes.nextTest: bookings, renewal economics and AI-security product adoption
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: keep PANW/CRWD high quality; wait for price rather than chase

themes.name: US LNG Diversification / Energy Security
themes.whyNow: Diversification from vulnerable supply routes remains structurally important, but the latest US-China meeting did not produce a verified LNG breakthrough and the immediate market is dominated by rates and refined products.
themes.marketTransmission: US gas, LNG contracting, Europe/Asia gas security, shipping
themes.confirmation: new SPAs, high utilization and durable international demand
themes.invalidation: weak contracting plus normalized competing supply/routes
themes.nextTest: new SPA/offtake announcements and China market access
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: LNG remains a high-quality entry candidate; no urgency chase

themes.name: Agriculture / Fertilizer / Food Affordability
themes.whyNow: Energy/diesel pressure worsens farm margins while input elasticity remains uneven. Premium genetics and nitrogen are harder to defer than potash/phosphate; machinery/irrigation remain more capex-cyclical.
themes.marketTransmission: food inflation, crop/input ratios, fertilizer volumes, farm cash flow, machinery demand
themes.confirmation: crop/input ratios and farmer margins improve without destroying core input volumes
themes.invalidation: farm economics force broad input cuts and capex deferral
themes.nextTest: crop prices, fertilizer, diesel, weather and acreage/input decisions
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: CTVA/NTR active-price research; CF wait for a base; BG/VMI background; AGCO second-stage only

themes.name: Uranium / Nuclear Fuel
themes.whyNow: Strategic baseload/fuel-cycle thesis remains intact, but no new contracting catalyst currently outranks rates, products or AI/grid. CCJ's falling tape improves valuation but still needs stabilization.
themes.marketTransmission: uranium contracting, conversion/enrichment, baseload power and data-centre power planning
themes.confirmation: long-term contracting, enrichment/conversion awards and project execution
themes.invalidation: utility contracting weakens materially or supply normalizes faster than demand
themes.nextTest: utility contracting/fuel-cycle awards and CCJ price stabilization
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: CCJ stays quality nuclear exposure but wait for a base/reclaim before increasing priority

themes.name: Robotics / Automation
themes.whyNow: Evidence still favors conventional industrial/warehouse automation and cobots over general-purpose humanoids. Chinese regulators are applying more discipline to humanoid IPOs while installed volumes remain small versus standard industrial robots.
themes.marketTransmission: industrial capex, warehouse productivity, machine vision, motion control, sensors, semiconductor equipment
themes.confirmation: repeat orders, utilization, margins and scaled commercial deployments
themes.nextTest: industrial orders and Hong Kong pricing/trading for new automation listings
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: favor profitable fixed/warehouse automation; RoboTechnik/humanoids research-only until pricing and economics prove out

themes.name: Precious Metals
themes.whyNow: Gold remains structurally supported by fiscal/geopolitical risk but is down on the week as the dollar and long yields rise. The current tape says rates dominate the hedge bid at the margin.
themes.marketTransmission: real/nominal yields, USD, fiscal risk, positioning
themes.confirmation: DXY and real/nominal yields roll over together while gold reclaims recent resistance
themes.nextTest: Treasury/Fed follow-through and gold response around recent support
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: no chase; wait for rate confirmation

themes.name: Grid ESS vs Lithium Overcapacity
themes.whyNow: Grid storage deployment is real, but generic cell/miner economics remain burdened by excess capacity. Downstream storage economics remain more investable than broad lithium beta.
themes.marketTransmission: BESS deployment, cell pricing, lithium margins, grid balancing
themes.confirmation: storage backlog, utilization and margins improve
themes.invalidation: deployment slows while cell/miner oversupply persists
themes.nextTest: storage bookings, margins and cell pricing
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: TSLA storage is the clearest bridge; generic lithium remains background
